chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from Imran al-Za'farani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever Allah favors with a bounty, and he comes at that time of the bounty with a clarinet (mizmar), he has denied it; and whoever is struck by a calamity, and he comes at that time of the calamity with a lamenter (na'ihah), he has denied it.
ai.seo_question: What constitutes ingratitude (kufr) in times of ease and hardship according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes a profound link between external expressions of emotion and internal spiritual states, defining ingratitude (kufr al-ni'mah) not merely as neglect of gratitude but as active denial through specific rituals. The use of the mizmar (a reed pipe) in times of ease is seen as a distraction that prevents recognition of the Divine source, while the professional naihah (lamenting woman) in hardship signifies a rejection of God's decree (qadr) and impatience with the trial. This concept is central to the Shia understanding of 'shukr' (gratitude) and 'sabr' (patience) as active, conscious acknowledgments rather than passive states.
